title: Labor markets and structural transformation in times of change: AI and demographic shifts
content_preview: Labor markets around the world are being reshaped by powerful trends, including rapid advances in artificial intelligence (AI), and population aging in some regions and youth bulges in others. AI's impact on labor markets is multifaceted and complex: It has the potential to create new job opportunities and make many jobs more productive, but it will also automate some tasks leading to the destruction of some of today's jobs. AI can also affect labor markets by changing international patterns of specialization. At the same time, demographic trends pose additional challenges. In all developed…

title: Mary E.  Lovely on what's really going on with global supply chains
content_preview: How have US tariffs affected global supply chains? Are trading patterns between countries really changing? What can we learn from the fine print of trade agreements? Bhatt in this episode, exploring Lovely's recent research on global supply chains and US "reciprocal" trade agreements. title: Many school supplies cost more under Trump's tariffs
content_preview: Autumn means back-to-school shopping for many households. This year, consumers face higher prices for many basic supplies because of President Donald Trump's tariffs. Backpacks, calculators, notebooks, and shoes are among the products in six categories hit with higher tariffs since he returned to the presidency in early 2025. Nationally, the annual tariff costs for these goods are projected to average $79 higher per US household this year than in 2024. title: The China Squeeze: A response to our critics
content_preview: Our recent PIIE working paper and the subsequent Foreign Affairs article detailed how China's manufacturing export strength is curbing poorer countries' opportunities to industrialize—what we call the China Squeeze.
